title: Sub-cell eigenmode descriptors for metamaterial homogenisation surrogates: code, descriptors, results and preprint
description:
Code, precomputed sub-cell elastodynamic eigenmode descriptors, complete experimental results and a venue-neutral preprint for a study of why machine-learned surrogates for the homogenised stiffness tensor C^H fail to transfer across unseen unit-cell topologies.

Classical homogenisation obtains C^H by volume-averaging the microscopic stress. Averaging is a projection: it retains the two rigid-translation modes of the unit cell and discards every other sub-cell degree of freedom. This record measures the discarded content by solving the Gamma-point elastodynamic eigenproblem on the same periodic operator that produces C^H. Four families in the benchmark have C11/C22 = 1.000 to machine precision, carrying no directional information, yet their sub-cell mode characters are well separated. Three numbers describing how the softest sub-cell mode divides its motion between rotation, dilatation and shear predict C22 on 18 unseen topological families at R2 = +0.356, where 2304 raw pixels give -0.008 and a free solid-fraction control gives +0.082, at a quarter of the cost of one homogenisation.

The deposit includes negative results as well as positive ones: the descriptor does not rescue a pixel surrogate, does not work as a training-family selection criterion, and an earlier per-eigenvector definition of mode character (also included) produced a false negative that is analysed in the preprint.

Requires only NumPy, SciPy, scikit-learn and Matplotlib; developed and run on a single CPU core. The unit-cell dataset is archived separately at doi 10.5281/zenodo.21734948.
